output.summary: A herbaceous perennial native to Europe and western Asia, it forms ground-covering mats with short upright shoots bearing soft violet flowers. It is sometimes grown as an edible herb, and its slightly bitter, astringent foliage was used as a tea substitute in 19th-century France.
output.edibilityNote: Sometimes grown as an edible herb; used as a tea substitute in 19th-century France because of its tea-like smell.
